title: Bracket a summary where lines are cut
statement: Abridge by cutting sections, keep the author's words for what stays, bridge each cut with a bracketed summary, and say the text is abridged and from which edition.
example: A planning meeting put the full opening scene at 15 minutes of reading.
detail: A Grade 9 unit plans one reading text per lesson, abridged from a named edition, with bracketed stage directions summarising the cut lines, and each reading text carries a line naming the edition it is abridged from and its licence. A planning meeting gave the reason: reading the full opening scene takes the full 15 minutes.
against: A classroom guide in the sources has learners do the cutting themselves, as close reading, and holds that "Students need and deserve the chance to tackle the real thing." (`g9/sources/Cutting-a-Scene-Othello-1.1.pdf`, pdftotext line 36). How far segments are abridged was left open in the planning meeting (`g9/library/collections/g3-repo-initiative-g9-othello-2026-10-01/MEETING-2026-10-01.md`, lines 49-50), and the draft abridgement still needed "edition attribution and non-commercial terms" confirmed (`g9/library/text/L7f7ca8.txt`, line 1).

evidence.quote: One reading doc per lesson, abridged from the Folger text, with stage directions in square brackets for the cut lines
